best_for: Artists, designers and students learning to code who want to draw with code in a small editor and see the result in a window right away.
description:
Processing is a free programming language and editor for making pictures, animation and interactive work with code. Ben Fry and Casey Reas started it in 2001. Contributors around the world develop it today, with support from the Processing Foundation.

Getting going takes three steps: open the app, pick an example, and press Run. Change a few numbers and run it again to see what happens. A shelf of books covers different goals and skill levels. Community-made libraries and tools add new abilities, and sites like OpenProcessing let you share what you make and see other people's sketches.

points.title: A sketchbook for learning code
points.text: Processing is a small editor and language built for learning to program through visual sketches. Hundreds of examples ship with the app, and the website adds tutorials and a full reference, so a beginner can open an example and change it within minutes.

points.title: Java mode first, more as add-ons
points.text: Java is the default mode. Other modes, libraries, tools and example packs install from managers inside the editor, such as Sketch, Import Library, Add Library. A finished sketch can be turned into a standalone program with File, Export Application.

points.title: Free, with one license catch
points.text: The editor is GPL-2.0 and the core library is LGPL-2.1, both free to use. The reference text is under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so you cannot reuse the documentation itself for commercial work.

points.title: Pick the right Mac build
points.text: On macOS there are separate disk images for Intel and Apple silicon Macs. Windows gets one x64 MSI that installs for the whole machine, plus a portable zip on GitHub. There is no Windows on Arm build.

points.title: Linux builds come from GitHub
points.text: This site lists only Windows and macOS. The project's GitHub release for 4.5.7 also carries .deb, Snap, Flatpak and portable zip builds for Linux on x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Few old versions here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 2 versions and macOS only the current release. Earlier Processing 4 releases are on GitHub, and 3.5.4 and older sit on a separate stable releases page linked from the download page.

points.title: Processing 5 is on the way
points.text: The project's GitHub README says work on Processing 5.0 is underway on the main branch, while Processing 4 receives bug fixes on its own branch. Sketches you write today run on the 4.x line.
